newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends higher with crude, rising demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends higher with crude, rising demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended modestly higher in very thin activity after a healthy rebound in crude oil futures and some signs of end-user demand, traders and brokers said.
June swaps rose $2.50 to $183.50/$184 and July rose the same amount to $180/$181. August swaps prices were flat to July.
NWE cargoes were notionally valued at $183/$185 cif.
The arbitrage from the Med to the Far East was closed but traders disagreed as to whether that would translate into more material ending up in Northwest Europe, and therefore lower prices.

"It's closed at the precise moment...but it's not a done deal that because it's closed then European prices will come off," said one trader. Sellers could still choose to offer their material out of Europe even with the arb shut out of the Med, he said.

"I think the sentiment as well as the physical market looks better than a couple of weeks ago," he said. He described the market as on the mildly bullish side of balanced, versus mildly bearish side earlier this month.
He said end-users were looking for material in the Med for the end of June and for high paraffinic material in Northwest Europe.
Two crackers were also in the processing of coming back on line, which was leading to more demand, he said.
